question.text: $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle \int -\dfrac{4}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, extrm d x=$
question.explanation:
$ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} $

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \int -\dfrac{4}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,\textrm d x =4\int -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \,\textrm d x =4\arsech{x}+C. \end{align*}

question.text: $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle \int -\dfrac{2}{x\sqrt{3\left(1-x^2 ight)}}\, extrm d x=$
question.explanation:
$ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} $

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \int -\dfrac{2}{x\sqrt{3\left(1-x^2\right)}}\,\textrm d x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3} \int -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \,\textrm d x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\arsech{x}+C. \end{align*}

question.text: $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x-x^3}-1}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, extrm d x=$
question.explanation:
$ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} $

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}. \]

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x-x^3}-1}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, \textrm d x & = \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x-x^3}}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, \textrm d x - \int \dfrac{1}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] & = \int \dfrac{\sqrt x\cdot\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, \textrm d x - \dfrac{1}{2} \int \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \, \textrm{d}x + \dfrac{1}{2}\int - \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{x} + \dfrac{1}{2}\arsech{x} + C . \end{align*}

question.text:
$ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} $

Calculate $\displaystyle \int -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi- \pi x^2}\, extrm d x$ for $|x|>1.$
question.explanation:
$ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} $ The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcoth x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \int -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi- \pi x^2}\,\textrm d x & = \int -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi(1 - x^2)} \,\textrm d x\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi} \int \dfrac{1}{1 - x^2} \,\textrm d x\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi}\arcoth{x}+C. \end{align*}

question.text:
$ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} $

Calculate $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{3}{(2-2x^2)}\, extrm d x$ for $|x|>1.$
question.explanation:
$ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} $ The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcoth x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \int \dfrac{3}{(2-2x^2)} \,\textrm d x =\dfrac{3}{2}\int \dfrac{1}{1-x^2} \,\textrm d x =\dfrac{3}{2}\arcoth{x}+C. \end{align*}
